_readme: Both calibration sets for the YC run (COLLECTION.md §4), pre-registered before any verdict or entry_stage writes. The answer key is external documents with citations, assembled independently of the judging protocol.

membership_traps._gate: zero false members at high confidence before any verdict writes

rows.name: Mercury
rows.basis: Immad Akhund founded Heyzap (YC W09) and was a YC part-time partner for W17; Mercury itself never did a batch and YC is not on the cap table (Series B led by Coatue).

stage_golden._taxonomy_ruling: A YC batch entry is Seed, not Pre-Seed. First-party basis: YC's own about page, sustained from at least 2009 to 2020 — 'Y Combinator provides seed funding for startups. Seed funding is the earliest stage of venture funding.' The 2005-2007 cheques were tiny ($6,000 per founder, capped near $20,000), which tempts a Pre-Seed answer, but YC's contemporaneous language calls it seed and the term did not exist. Pre-Seed and Series A are STRUCTURALLY EMPTY for this investor: Continuity's mandate was pro rata and later-stage growth, so it never led a Series A.
stage_golden._scoring: Raw accuracy is close to meaningless here: 30 of 32 rows are Seed, so answering 'Seed' unconditionally scores 94%. Score by class instead. Class A (2 rows, Convoy and Monzo) is the only place the LABEL itself discriminates and is binary and unforgiving. Class B (11 rows) answers Seed while dangling a large publicised Continuity round — a Growth answer there is the same error as missing class A, with eleven chances to catch it. Class C (9 rows) answers Seed against a famous Sequoia/USV/IVP Series A and tests round identification. Class D (10 controls) should be free; a Pre-Seed answer on the 2005-2008 rows means the judge is reasoning from cheque size rather than from YC's own framing.

_batch_deal_eras.2005-2006: $6,000 per founder, rarely more than $20,000 total, 5-7%
_batch_deal_eras.2010-2014: $11,000 + $3,000 per founder plus an automatic outside note: $150k Start Fund (Jan 2011-Nov 2012), then $80k YC VC (from Nov 2012)
_batch_deal_eras.2022-01 onward: $500,000 total: $125k for 7% post-money SAFE + $375k uncapped MFN SAFE (https://www.ycombinator.com/deal)
